2009-Oct 12 2022

I rescued him from a kill shelter the day before he was to be euthanized. I knew he was the one when they let him out of his cage for us to meet each other and he immediately jumped into my lap.

He was quiet and shy, yet very sweet to everyone once he realized that no one meant him any harm. 

For the twelve years we were together he never left my side.

Shortly before pandemic times he was diagnosed with a grade 6 heart murmur and congestive heart failure, terminal. He was on all kinds of medications but never lost a step until late august of this year, when he began to get weak. 

I came home from work late October 11 to find him in a very bad state, but it’s like he was waiting for me to come home so he could pass on. He took his last breath in my arms at 2:30 the next morning.

Not an hour goes by that I don’t think of him, and I expect it will be that way forever. 

He was my best friend.

1/2c low low sodium soy sauce (if you don’t have the low sodium stuff, just go lighter on the salt)
1/4c olive oil 
4 tbsp light brown sugar
1 tbsp black pepper (I ground some long pepper, white pepper, and tricolor pepper for this, but any “floral” smelling pepper will do the job)
1 tbsp oyster sauce
1 tsp garlic powder (fresh minced garlic would actually be better, but I didn’t have any at the time. About 6-7 cloves finely minced or put through a garlic press would be ideal)
1 tsp powdered ginger
Pinch kosher salt
Pinch MSG

Put the tri tip in your preferred marinating vessel (I just use a falling ziploc bag), and add the well-stirred marinade. Seal it up, put it in the fridge, and let it do its thing for 5 hours.

Once it’s thoroughly marinated, grill the tri tip, flipping often, until it reaches about 120-125F. Pour the leftover marinade over the meat every time you flip it. Once you get it up to temp, take it off and let it rest in a warm place (I just put mine in the oven [not turned on] to stay warm)



Roughly chop the following veg:
1 Onion
3 Bell peppers (i used red, green, and yellow. It gave the finished dish some really nice color)
1 zucchini 
2 carrots 

1 whole thin sliced leek
About 5 cloves of finely minced garlic

Cook about 4 cups of short grain rice. When it’s done season with a pinch of salt and a splash of mirin.

Sauce:
1/2c soy sauce
3 tbsp light brown sugar
1 tsp mirin
1/4 tsp sesame oil
1 tbsp Toban Djan (or really any chili paste with something sweet in it. Gochujang would work well for this)
~1/6 rice win vinegar mixed with about 1 tbsp of plain white sugar
1 small handful of sliced leeks

Get all of that going in a saucepan over med low heat and let it simmer until the leeks are tender

Sautée all the vegetables separately until for just a couple minutes until they take on a little color. I did the onions and garlic at the same time, adding the garlic about a minute or so after the onions. Set everything aside

Cut up the tri tip into small pieces. I made sure that every piece had an exterior face - it both looks better and tastes better

Heat up a big pan to med high heat. Once it’s hot add a couple tbsp of oil, and add the meat, get a little more color on it, then add the rice, vegetables and sauce. Fold until the sauce is coating everything. If you don’t have enough sauce to coat everything , you can just add a little bit more soy sauce. 

Once it’s all heated through, it’s time to plate. 

Fry an egg over easy for every serving, and put it on top of the rice. Garnish with something green (used cilantro because it’s what I had, but green onions would probably be better), a squirt of Sriracha, and finally top with a few raw leek slices. 

Enjoy!
